name: shelter
_note: A built shelter is local. The discovered beach rocks already provide natural shelter.
hint: A simple habitation of leaning logs. Away from the beach's natural rock shelter, build this before placing a bed.

log: You lean logs into a frame and pack the gaps with branches.
Log by log, a lean-to rises. You pack the gaps against the wind.
You wedge the logs together until the wind cannot get in.

name: bed
hint: A bed raised above the ground. Under shelter, with a fire, retiring before midnight restores 100% energy.

build.label: make
log: You lash two logs into a frame and heap it with springy branches.
You assemble a low wooden frame and cover it thickly with boughs.
A narrow bed of timber and branches now raises you above the cold ground.

name: drying rack
hint: A rack on which fish or meat dries for 12 hours. Process one batch at a time; use meat's dry action to hang it.

log: You drive two logs into the sand by the fire and lay a third across them.
Two uprights, a crossbar: a rack beside the fire, where the smoke drifts.
You erect the rack downwind of the hearth, where fish and meat may dry slowly.

start.label: hang fish
log: You clean and split two fish before hanging them from the crossbar.
Two prepared fish are suspended on the rack to dry.
You arrange the fish where the rising smoke can reach them.

collect.label: take down
log: The preserved food has become firm and dark during its time above the fire.
Dry, hard, smelling of smoke. They will keep.
The food leaves the rack thoroughly dry, and should now keep far longer.

readyLog: The food upon the rack has become sufficiently dry for storage.
The provisions have finished drying and may now be collected.

name: rain barrel
hint: A vessel hollowed from timber and placed beneath the eaves. Rain fills it in 12 hours.

log: You hollow a log with the axe and set it under the edge of the shelter.
Hour by hour the axe hollows the log.
The hollow trunk is set upright beneath the eaves, ready for the next shower.

start.label: set out
log: You place the barrel beneath the shelter's dripping edge.
The vessel stands ready where the next rain will gather.

collect.label: drink
log: You drink the cold rainwater accumulated in the wooden vessel.
The water carries a faint taste of timber, but it is fresh and welcome.
A useful store of rainwater is now at your disposal.

name: fish trap
_note: anywhere you can fish: the shallows, the river. 1 fish every 2 hours, up to 3; stays set
hint: A trap of woven willow, yielding 1 fish every 2 hours, up to 3. Once placed, it remains set.

log: You weave the willow into a long basket with a funnel at the mouth.
You weave willow into a trap with a narrow, one-way entrance.
You bend and weave the willow until you have a trap with a narrow mouth.

start.label: set
log: You secure the trap in the current with stones, its entrance facing upstream.
The woven basket is lowered into a channel frequented by fish.
A heavy stone holds the trap in place beneath the running water.

collect.label: empty
log: You draw the trap from the stream, water streaming between its willow ribs.
The basket rises heavily from the current; something moves within.
You lift the dripping trap for examination.

readyLog: A sudden movement within the woven trap suggests a catch.
The basket stirs in the current; a fish has apparently entered.

name: snares
hint: Running nooses arranged across animal paths. Inspect them after 12 hours.

build.label: make
log: You fashion running nooses of cord and fix them across the narrow animal tracks.
Nooses of cord, pegged a hand above the ground where the trails narrow.
The snares are carefully knotted and pegged along the familiar rabbit runs.

start.label: set
log: You reset the nooses and smooth away the signs of your presence.
The snares are opened anew, and you retreat quietly from the trails.
You examine each cord and stake before leaving the traps undisturbed.

collect.label: check

text: One snare holds a rabbit, already cold and still.
A rabbit has been taken in the running noose.
Your last snare contains a rabbit: the labour has not been wasted.
One noose has been dragged loose, but no animal remains.
Every snare is empty upon inspection.
Tracks surround the traps, yet none has secured its quarry.

log: You follow the narrow trails, examining each snare in turn.
One by one the running nooses are checked for a catch.
You move quietly between the traps, looking for signs of success.

name: corn field
hint: A plot of cultivated ground. Seed sown here produces ripe corn in 3 days.

build.label: dig
log: You turn the soil with the hoe and place the kernels carefully in ordered rows.
Hours of hacking at the turf.
The hoe turns the soil over in long rows.

start.label: sow
log: You prepare the furrows afresh and sow another crop.
Each kernel is placed in the soil at a suitable interval.
Having sown the rows, you cover the grain carefully with earth.

collect.label: harvest
log: You break the ripe ears from their stalks and gather them together.
The dry leaves rustle as you collect the harvest.
The field yields ear after ear of corn, carried away in your arms.

readyLog: The corn has reached maturity and may be harvested.
The ears of corn have filled out; the crop is ripe.

name: bee hive
hint: A hollow log for wild bees. Gather honey every 3 days, after quieting the insects with smoke.

log: You hollow a log and stand it among the flowers, a hand-width hole near the top.
A hollow log, capped with bark, set on stones among the flowers.

start.label: lure bees
log: You smear the hive entrance with crushed berries to attract the wandering bees.
Berry juice is applied around the hollow's opening.
The sweet scent of crushed berries draws the insects towards the prepared log.

collect.label: take honey
log: With smoke to quiet the bees, you remove a portion of their honeycomb.
You work slowly among the drowsy insects and secure a dripping piece of comb.
Smoke makes the bees less active, allowing you to take a share of their honey.

name: fish weir
hint: A barrier of stakes and stones across the current. It collects fish every 12 hours.

log: You build a stone-and-stake barrier across the river.
Stone by stone, a low wall grows across the river.
A fence of stones and stakes across the river, with one narrow way through.

start.label: close
log: You close the passage with a woven mat of willow.
You block the weir's gap. The fish can come in, not out.

collect.label: empty
log: You enter the shallow pool above the barrier and take the confined fish by hand.
The weir has gathered fish behind its stones, from which you remove them.
Within the enclosed water the fish have little room to escape.

name: campfire
hint: A prepared hearth in this area. Kindle it with matches, stones, or dry sticks, then maintain it with wood.

build.log: You arrange stones in a ring and clear a safe place for a fire.
